raw_response:
*Sits down with a cup of tea, thinking about the season ahead.*

Well, I've been working these 5 mu for forty years now, and cotton has been my main crop for most of that time. My wife and I are the only ones left at home — the kids are in the city — so labor is my biggest worry every year, not the agronomy. I know the agronomy. What I can't do anymore is pick 5 mu of cotton by myself in October like I did at 40.

Let me think through this season.

**Land prep and planting.** I turned the soil with the plow last November after last year's cotton stalks came out, and I'll hire the rotary tiller (旋耕机) for about 50 yuan/mu in early April. I'll lay plastic mulch (地膜) — everybody here does, it warms the soil and saves water, and at my age I'm not going to fight that battle. I plant mid-to-late April when the 5-cm soil temperature is steady above 14°C for a few days. If it's a cold spring I wait; rushing cotton into cold ground is how you get poor stands and then you're replanting, which costs me seed and time I don't have.

**Seed.** I buy new hybrid Bt cotton every year — something like 鲁棉研 or a local hybrid that the agrotech station recommends. Saving cotton seed is false economy; the F2 generation loses vigor and the Bt protection weakens. About 40-50 yuan/mu for good seed, and I use a hand planter with one of my neighbors. Density around 3,500 plants/mu — a bit lower than the young farmers push, because at my density I get bigger bolls and less mirid bug pressure, and it's easier to manage at my age.

**Fertilizer.** With 40 years on this soil, I know my fields. Some organic matter from the stalks, OK but not rich. I target about 260 kg/mu of seed cotton, which for me means:
- Base before mulching: 50 kg/mu of 15-15-15 compound (so 7.5 kg each of N, P₂O₅, K₂O)
- Topdress at initial flowering (初花期), around early-mid July: about 15 kg/mu urea = 6.9 kg N
- A second topdress at peak bolling if the crop looks hungry: maybe 8 kg/mu urea = 3.7 kg N

Total roughly 18 kg N/mu, 7.5 kg P₂O₅, 7.5 kg K₂O. Cotton likes potassium for boll filling — I learned that the hard way in the 1990s when I skimped on K and got a lot of premature opening. The compound covers it. I don't skimp anymore.

**Irrigation.** My well is metered. I budget for:
1. Pre-planting "tamping water" (塌墒水) if the winter was dry — sometimes skipped if soil moisture is good
2. Initial flowering irrigation in early July
3. Peak flowering/bolling in late July to mid-August, this is the non-negotiable one
4. A light one in early September if it's a drought year

So 2-3 irrigations typically, 4 in a dry year. Cotton is not thirsty like maize — too much water and you get rank growth and boll rot.

**Pesticides.** This is where cotton eats money. Even with Bt, I spray:
- Pre-emergence herbicide (乙草胺/acetochlor) under the mulch
- Aphid control in June (imidacloprid or similar) — once or twice
- Mirid bugs (盲蝽) in July-August — 2-3 sprays, they're my real enemy now that bollworm is mostly handled by the Bt
- Spider mites if July is hot and dry
- Maybe a fungicide if I see verticillium wilt (黄萎病) starting

I don't spray on a calendar. I walk the fields every few days and decide. Forty years of looking at cotton leaves — I know what I'm seeing.

**Topping (打顶).** Manual, around late July, remove the terminal bud to stop vertical growth and push energy into bolls. For 5 mu my wife and I can do this in two days. I also use a growth regulator (缩节胺/mepiquat chloride) two or three times to control canopy — this is one of the technical things I picked up from the extension training in the 2000s and it really pays off.

**Harvest and labor.** This is the hard part. Picking starts late September, runs through October, sometimes into November. For 5 mu at 260 kg/mu that's 1,300 kg of seed cotton to pick by hand. My wife and I can maybe do 30 kg/day together at our age — that's 43 person-days. Too much. I'll hire 2-3 women from the village for 10-12 days at peak picking, around 120-150 yuan/day each. That's my single biggest cash expense.

**Yield and price.** I'm targeting 260 kg/mu seed cotton. Last year I got 255, year before 270. Price at the gin last year was around 7 yuan/kg for seed cotton, but prices have been volatile — I watch but I can't predict. Gross revenue roughly 260 × 7 × 5 = 9,100 yuan. After inputs (~3,800 yuan) and my time, the margin is thin but this land has been in the family and I know nothing else.
